quote: I wanted you to see what real courage is, instead of getting the idea that courage is a man with a gun in his hand. It’s when you know you’re licked before you begin but you begin anyway and you see it through no matter what.
source: Harper Lee, To Kill a Mockingbird, ch. 11, to Jem after Mrs Dubose (Atticus Finch) (1960)
speaker: Atticus Finch

evidence.where: A full text of Part One, chapter 11 was read. Atticus says to Jem: I wanted you to see what real courage is, instead of getting the idea that courage is a man with a gun in his hand. It's when you know you're licked before you begin but you begin anyway and you see it through no matter what. You rarely win, but sometimes you do. Mrs. Dubose won, all ninety-eight pounds of her. The two sentences the proposal takes are consecutive and complete, and match that text word for word, including the absence of a comma before but you begin anyway, which several study editions insert. The occasion is right: Atticus speaks after Mrs Dubose's death, explaining what Jem's reading aloud to her was for. A printed Lippincott copy was not opened, so the source names the year of first publication and no publisher.
